IMPLEMENT THIS EXACT APPROVED LESSON CONTENT:

SUBJECT:
Science

GRADE:
Grade 1

LESSON:
Lesson 4

TITLE:
Weather ☀️🌧️

SUBTITLE:
Learn how to observe weather, describe daily conditions, and choose what to wear or do safely.

ESTIMATED TIME:
20–25 minutes

==================================================
LEARNING GOALS 🎯
==================================================

By the end of this lesson, the learner should be able to:

• Describe common kinds of weather.
• Identify sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, and stormy conditions.
• Recognize that weather can change from day to day.
• Use simple observations to describe the weather.
• Choose suitable clothing or activities for different weather.
• Follow basic weather safety rules.

==================================================
OPENING — WHAT IS THE WEATHER LIKE TODAY? 👀
==================================================

Look outside.

What do you notice?

Is the Sun shining brightly? ☀️

Are there many clouds? ☁️

Is rain falling? 🌧️

Are tree branches moving in the wind? 🌬️

Weather describes what the air and sky are like in a place at a certain time.

Weather can be:

☀️ sunny;

☁️ cloudy;

🌧️ rainy;

🌬️ windy;

⛈️ stormy;

or a mixture of different conditions.

Weather can change.

A morning may begin sunny and later become cloudy or rainy.

That is why we observe the weather regularly.

==================================================
SECTION 1 — SUNNY WEATHER ☀️
==================================================

A sunny day usually has plenty of sunlight.

The sky may look bright and mostly clear.

Sunlight can make the day feel warm.

On a sunny day, people may:

🧢 wear a hat;

💧 drink water;

🌳 spend time in shaded areas;

🧴 use sun protection with adult guidance.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------------------

You look outside and see:

• a bright sky;
• strong sunlight;
• only a few clouds.

You could describe the weather as:

☀️ Sunny

==================================================
VISUAL 1 — SUNNY WEATHER
==================================================

Create a bright child-friendly weather scene.

Show:

☀️ Sun
🌤️ mostly clear sky
🌳 tree
🧒 child wearing a hat
💧 water bottle

Caption:

"Sunny weather has plenty of sunlight."

==================================================
SECTION 2 — CLOUDY WEATHER ☁️
==================================================

Cloudy weather happens when many clouds cover part or much of the sky.

Clouds are made of tiny drops of water or ice high in the atmosphere.

Some clouds are thin and white.

Others can look thick and gray.

A cloudy day does not always mean it will rain.

But some clouds can bring rain.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------------------

You look outside.

The Sun is hard to see because many clouds cover the sky.

You could describe the weather as:

☁️ Cloudy

==================================================
SECTION 3 — RAINY WEATHER 🌧️
==================================================

Rain happens when drops of water fall from clouds.

Rain gives water to plants and helps fill rivers, ponds, and other water sources.

When it rains, people may use:

☔ umbrellas;

🧥 raincoats;

🥾 boots.

Roads and paths can become wet and slippery.

We should walk carefully.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------------------

You hear drops hitting the roof.

Water is falling from the sky.

People are carrying umbrellas.

The weather is:

🌧️ Rainy

==================================================
VISUAL 2 — RAINY WEATHER
==================================================

Create a simple rainy-day scene.

Show:

🌧️ rain cloud
☔ umbrella
🧥 raincoat
💧 puddles

Caption:

"Rain is water that falls from clouds."

==================================================
SECTION 4 — WINDY WEATHER 🌬️
==================================================

Wind is moving air.

We cannot usually see the air itself.

But we can see what the wind moves.

On a windy day, you might notice:

🍃 leaves moving;

🌳 branches swaying;

🚩 flags waving;

🪁 kites flying.

A little wind can feel pleasant.

Very strong winds can be dangerous.

--------------------------------------------------
HOW CAN WE TELL IT IS WINDY?
--------------------------------------------------

Look for things that are moving because of the air.

For example:

A flag is flapping.

Leaves are blowing across the ground.

Tree branches are moving.

These are clues that the weather is windy.

==================================================
VISUAL 3 — HOW WE NOTICE WIND
==================================================

Create a simple visual showing:

🚩 waving flag
🍃 blowing leaves
🌳 moving branches
🪁 kite

Add arrows to show the direction of moving air.

Caption:

"We cannot see wind itself, but we can see what it moves."

==================================================
SECTION 5 — STORMY WEATHER ⛈️
==================================================

A storm may bring:

🌧️ heavy rain;

🌬️ strong wind;

⚡ lightning;

🌩️ thunder;

dark clouds.

Stormy weather can be dangerous.

When there is thunder or lightning, children should follow instructions from trusted adults and stay in a safe place.

--------------------------------------------------
IMPORTANT SAFETY RULE ⚠️
--------------------------------------------------

If you hear thunder:

Go indoors or stay inside a safe building.

Do not stay in an open field.

Do not shelter under a lone tree.

Follow adult instructions.

==================================================
SECTION 6 — WEATHER CAN CHANGE 🔄
==================================================

Weather does not stay exactly the same every day.

Monday may be sunny.

Tuesday may be rainy.

Wednesday may be cloudy.

Weather can even change during the same day.

For example:

Morning:
☀️ Sunny

Afternoon:
☁️ Cloudy

Later:
🌧️ Rainy

Because weather can change, people observe it often.

==================================================
VISUAL 4 — WEATHER CAN CHANGE
==================================================

Create a simple timeline:

Morning
☀️ Sunny

↓

Afternoon
☁️ Cloudy

↓

Evening
🌧️ Rainy

Caption:

"Weather can change during the day."

==================================================
SECTION 7 — HOW DO WE DESCRIBE WEATHER? 🔎
==================================================

We can describe weather by observing different things.

Ask:

What does the sky look like?

Is the Sun easy to see?

Are clouds covering the sky?

Is rain falling?

Is the wind moving leaves or flags?

Does the air feel warm or cool?

These observations help us describe the weather.

==================================================
SECTION 8 — TEMPERATURE 🌡️
==================================================

Temperature tells us how warm or cool something is.

We often describe the weather as:

🔥 hot;

🙂 warm;

❄️ cool;

🥶 cold.

A thermometer is a tool used to measure temperature.

For Grade 1, the important idea is:

🌡️ A thermometer helps us measure how warm or cold the air is.

==================================================
VISUAL 5 — HOT, WARM, COOL, COLD
==================================================

Create a simple vertical thermometer-style visual.

Top:
🔥 Hot

Below:
☀️ Warm

Below:
🍃 Cool

Bottom:
❄️ Cold

Do not require Grade 1 students to memorize complicated temperature scales in this lesson.

Caption:

"Temperature tells us how warm or cold the air is."

==================================================
SECTION 9 — WEATHER TOOLS 🧰
==================================================

People use tools to observe and measure weather.

For Grade 1, introduce these simple tools:

--------------------------------------------------
THERMOMETER 🌡️
--------------------------------------------------

Measures temperature.

--------------------------------------------------
RAIN GAUGE 🌧️
--------------------------------------------------

Measures how much rain falls.

--------------------------------------------------
WIND VANE 🌬️
--------------------------------------------------

Shows the direction the wind is coming from.

--------------------------------------------------
ANEMOMETER 💨
--------------------------------------------------

Measures wind speed.

Do not expect Grade 1 students to memorize every tool perfectly.

The main idea is:

"Scientists use tools to measure weather."

==================================================
VISUAL 6 — SIMPLE WEATHER TOOLS
==================================================

Create a four-card visual:

🌡️ Thermometer
Measures temperature

🌧️ Rain gauge
Measures rainfall

🧭 Wind vane
Shows wind direction

💨 Anemometer
Measures wind speed

Use simple drawings and short labels.

==================================================
SECTION 10 — CLOUDS CAN GIVE US CLUES ☁️
==================================================

Clouds are an important part of weather.

A few small white clouds may appear on a fair day.

Thicker gray clouds may bring rain.

But looking at clouds alone does not always tell us exactly what will happen.

Weather can change.

We observe several clues together.

💡 REMEMBER:

One cloud does not always mean rain is coming.

==================================================
SECTION 11 — WEATHER AND CLOTHING 👕
==================================================

Weather can help us decide what clothing may be useful.

--------------------------------------------------
SUNNY AND HOT ☀️
--------------------------------------------------

You might choose:

👕 light clothing;

🧢 a hat;

💧 water.

--------------------------------------------------
RAINY 🌧️
--------------------------------------------------

You might choose:

🧥 raincoat;

☔ umbrella;

🥾 boots.

--------------------------------------------------
COOL OR COLD ❄️
--------------------------------------------------

You might choose:

🧥 jacket;

🧣 warm clothing.

The goal is to dress in a way that helps you stay comfortable and safe.

==================================================
SECTION 12 — WEATHER AND ACTIVITIES ⚽
==================================================

Weather can affect what activities are suitable.

A calm sunny day might be good for:

⚽ outdoor games;

🚲 cycling with proper safety equipment;

🌳 visiting a park.

A rainy day may be better for:

📚 reading indoors;

🎨 drawing;

🧩 puzzles.

Stormy weather may mean:

🏠 staying safely indoors.

We should always choose activities that fit the weather and follow adult safety instructions.

==================================================
WORKED EXAMPLE — WHAT IS THE WEATHER? 🔎
==================================================

Imagine you look outside.

You observe:

• dark clouds;
• water falling from the sky;
• people using umbrellas;
• puddles forming on the ground.

Let's decide what kind of weather this is.

STEP 1:
Look at the sky.

There are dark clouds.

STEP 2:
Look for precipitation.

Water is falling from the sky.

STEP 3:
Look at what people are doing.

People are using umbrellas.

CONCLUSION:

🌧️ The weather is rainy.

==================================================
GUIDED EXAMPLE — IS IT WINDY? 🌬️
==================================================

You cannot see air.

But you notice:

🍃 leaves blowing;

🚩 a flag waving quickly;

🌳 small branches moving.

What does this tell you?

The air is moving.

So the weather is:

🌬️ Windy

==================================================
SECTION 13 — WEATHER OR SEASON? 🤔
==================================================

Weather describes conditions over a short time.

For example:

"Today is rainy."

"Tomorrow may be sunny."

A season lasts much longer.

Different places have different seasonal patterns.

For Grade 1, remember:

WEATHER:
what the air and sky are like now or over a short time.

SEASON:
a longer part of the year with common weather patterns.

Do not mix up weather with seasons.

==================================================
SECTION 14 — WEATHER SAFETY 🛡️
==================================================

Weather can be fun to observe, but safety is important.

--------------------------------------------------
HOT AND SUNNY WEATHER ☀️
--------------------------------------------------

Drink water.

Take breaks in shade.

Follow adult guidance for sun protection.

--------------------------------------------------
RAINY WEATHER 🌧️
--------------------------------------------------

Walk carefully on wet surfaces.

Stay away from fast-moving floodwater.

Never play in flooded areas.

--------------------------------------------------
THUNDERSTORMS ⛈️
--------------------------------------------------

Go inside a safe building.

Stay away from open areas.

Follow adult instructions.

--------------------------------------------------
STRONG WIND 🌬️
--------------------------------------------------

Stay away from loose objects or branches that may fall.

Move to a safe place if adults tell you to.

==================================================
SECTION 15 — WEATHER CAN AFFECT LIVING THINGS 🌱🐾
==================================================

Weather affects plants, animals, and people.

Plants may receive water from rain. 🌱💧

Animals may look for shade when it is very hot. 🐕🌳

Birds may seek shelter during strong rain. 🐦

People choose clothing and activities based on weather.

Weather is part of the environment around living things.

==================================================
ACTIVITY — WHAT WEATHER DO YOU SEE? 👀
==================================================

Imagine these scenes.

--------------------------------------------------

SCENE 1

Bright Sun
Blue sky
Very few clouds

Weather:
☀️ Sunny

--------------------------------------------------

SCENE 2

Water falling
Umbrellas open

Weather:
🌧️ Rainy

--------------------------------------------------

SCENE 3

Flag waving
Leaves blowing
Branches moving

Weather:
🌬️ Windy

--------------------------------------------------

SCENE 4

Dark clouds
Heavy rain
Thunder and lightning

Weather:
⛈️ Stormy

==================================================
ACTIVITY — WHAT SHOULD YOU BRING? 🎒
==================================================

RAINY DAY 🌧️

Useful:
☔ Umbrella

--------------------------------------------------

SUNNY HOT DAY ☀️

Useful:
🧢 Hat
💧 Water

--------------------------------------------------

COOL DAY 🍃

Useful:
🧥 Jacket

--------------------------------------------------

STORMY DAY ⛈️

Best choice:
🏠 Stay safely indoors and follow adult instructions.

==================================================
COMMON MISTAKES ⚠️
==================================================

MISTAKE 1:

"Cloudy always means it is raining."

❌ Not true.

A day can be cloudy without rain.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 2:

"If I cannot see the wind, it is not there."

❌ Not true.

Wind is moving air.

We can observe what it moves.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 3:

"Weather stays the same all day."

❌ Not always.

Weather can change during the day.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 4:

"Every sunny day has no clouds."

❌ Not true.

A sunny day can still have some clouds.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 5:

"Thunderstorms are safe to play outside in."

❌ Not true.

Thunder and lightning can be dangerous.

We should go to a safe indoor place and follow adult instructions.

==================================================
QUICK CHECK 🧠
==================================================

1. THE SUN IS BRIGHT AND THE SKY IS MOSTLY CLEAR.

Weather:
Sunny ☀️

Why?
There is plenty of sunlight and few clouds.

--------------------------------------------------

2. WATER IS FALLING FROM CLOUDS.

Weather:
Rainy 🌧️

Why?
Rain is falling from the sky.

--------------------------------------------------

3. LEAVES AND FLAGS ARE MOVING QUICKLY.

Weather:
Windy 🌬️

Why?
Moving air is pushing them.

--------------------------------------------------

4. WHICH TOOL MEASURES TEMPERATURE?

Answer:
Thermometer 🌡️

Why?
A thermometer measures how warm or cold the air is.

--------------------------------------------------

5. YOU HEAR THUNDER OUTSIDE.

What should you do?

Answer:
Go to a safe indoor place. 🏠

Why?
Thunderstorms can be dangerous.

==================================================
KEY CONCEPT ⭐
==================================================

TITLE:

Weather tells us what the air and sky are like.

BODY:

Weather can be sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, stormy, warm, cool, and more.

We can observe the sky, rain, wind, and temperature to describe weather.

Weather can change, so we observe it regularly.

==================================================
FINAL RECAP 🌟
==================================================

Remember:

☀️ Sunny weather has plenty of sunlight.

☁️ Cloudy weather has many clouds.

🌧️ Rainy weather has water falling from clouds.

🌬️ Windy weather has moving air.

⛈️ Stormy weather may bring heavy rain, strong wind, thunder, or lightning.

🌡️ Temperature tells us how warm or cold the air is.

🔄 Weather can change during the day.

👕 Weather helps us choose suitable clothing.

🛡️ We should follow safety rules during dangerous weather.

QUIZ RULES FOR THIS LESSON
==================================================

The separate Lesson 4 quiz must contain:

20 questions.

GRADE 1 RULE:
MULTIPLE CHOICE ONLY.

Do NOT create:

• identification;
• fill-in-the-blank;
• typed answer;
• free response.

Questions must come ONLY from this lesson's domain.

Allowed quiz concepts include:

• sunny weather
• cloudy weather
• rainy weather
• windy weather
• stormy weather
• simple weather observations
• changing weather
• temperature
• thermometer
• basic weather tools
• appropriate clothing
• suitable activities
• weather safety
• weather effects on living things
• difference between weather and season at the simple Grade 1 level

Question progression:

1–7:
basic recognition

8–14:
understanding and matching

15–20:
simple reasoning and real-life application

Also create:

3 mastery challenge questions.

All mastery challenge questions must also be:

MULTIPLE CHOICE ONLY.

==================================================
QUIZ ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Avoid ambiguous weather questions.

BAD:

"What weather is best?"

There may be no single correct answer.

GOOD:

"Water is falling from clouds. Which weather condition is being described?"

Answer:
Rainy

BAD:

"What should you wear outside?"

This depends on weather.

GOOD:

"It is raining outside. Which item would be most useful?"

Answer:
Umbrella

For wind questions, do not say that we "see wind."

Instead, ask about evidence such as:

• moving leaves;
• waving flags;
• swaying branches.

For storm safety:

Do not include unsafe answers that could accidentally sound acceptable.

Correct guidance should emphasize:

• moving indoors;
• following trusted adult instructions;
• avoiding open areas during thunderstorms.
